# SSGOI setup guide

SSGOI adds route transitions without replacing the application router.

Current core version: `@ssgoi/core@7.0.0-beta.0`

## Contents

1. Next.js setup
2. Route boundary contract
3. Persistent layouts
4. Sliding tabs
5. Bottom navigation and route groups
6. Transition config
7. Transition index
8. Other frameworks
9. Troubleshooting

## 1. Next.js setup

```bash
npm install @ssgoi/react
```

Keep one config and one `<Ssgoi>` above all route boundaries.

```tsx
// app/ssgoi-provider.tsx
"use client";

import { Ssgoi } from "@ssgoi/react";
import { drill, slide, zoom } from "@ssgoi/react/view-transitions";

const productPaths = [
  "/products/all",
  "/products/electronics",
  "/products/fashion",
];

const config = {
  preserveScroll: { exclude: ["/posts/*"] },
  transitions: [
    { on: "/posts/**", except: "/posts", transition: drill() },
    {
      ordered: productPaths,
      transition: slide(),
    },
    {
      from: "/gallery",
      to: "/gallery/:id",
      transition: zoom({ type: "expand" }),
    },
  ],
};

export function SsgoiProvider({ children }) {
  return <Ssgoi config={config}>{children}</Ssgoi>;
}
```

```tsx
// app/layout.tsx
import { SsgoiProvider } from "./ssgoi-provider";

export default function RootLayout({ children }) {
  return (
    <html>
      <body>
        <main className="relative z-0 min-h-dvh overflow-x-clip">
          <SsgoiProvider>{children}</SsgoiProvider>
        </main>
      </body>
    </html>
  );
}
```

Layout requirements:

- `relative`: positions the outgoing page.
- `z-0`: creates a local stacking context.
- `overflow-x-clip`: prevents horizontal overflow during slide and drill.

## 2. Route boundary contract

SSGOI does not provide a router-aware boundary. Create one for the application.

```tsx
// app/ssgoi-transition-boundary.tsx
"use client";

import {
  type ElementType,
  type Key,
  type ReactNode,
} from "react";
import { usePathname } from "next/navigation";

type BoundaryScope = (pathname: string) => Key;

const pathnameScope: BoundaryScope = (pathname) => pathname;

export function SsgoiTransitionBoundary({
  children,
  as,
  className,
  scope = pathnameScope,
}: {
  children: ReactNode;
  as?: ElementType;
  className?: string;
  scope?: BoundaryScope;
}) {
  const pathname = usePathname();
  const Component = as ?? "div";

  return (
    <Component
      key={scope(pathname)}
      data-ssgoi-transition={pathname}
      className={className}
    >
      {children}
    </Component>
  );
}
```

The two values have different jobs:

- `key`: controls layout lifetime.
- `data-ssgoi-transition`: identifies the real route for config matching.

Returning the same scope key prevents a remount:

```tsx
<SsgoiTransitionBoundary
  scope={(pathname) =>
    pathname.startsWith("/products/")
      ? "products-layout"
      : pathname
  }
>
  {children}
</SsgoiTransitionBoundary>
```

Do not put one pathname-keyed boundary around the entire application. Put
boundaries in the layouts that own the UI region being animated.

## 3. Persistent layouts

Use one outer stable boundary and one inner pathname boundary.

```tsx
export default function ProductsLayout({ children }) {
  return (
    <SsgoiTransitionBoundary scope={() => "products-layout"}>
      <ProductHeader />
      <ProductTabs />

      <SsgoiTransitionBoundary>
        {children}
      </SsgoiTransitionBoundary>
    </SsgoiTransitionBoundary>
  );
}
```

- Product category change: outer layout stays; inner content remounts.
- Leaving products: outer layout and its chrome leave together.
- Entering products: the outer layout owns the incoming transition.

When nested boundaries change in one DOM mutation, SSGOI uses the outer changed
boundary. A nested boundary owns a transition only while its parent remains
mounted.

## 4. Sliding tabs

Use `ordered` to define direction.

```ts
const config = {
  transitions: [
    {
      ordered: [
        "/products/all",
        "/products/electronics",
        "/products/fashion",
      ],
      transition: slide(),
    },
  ],
};
```

Increasing index is forward. Decreasing index is backward.

The tab header belongs outside the inner pathname boundary:

```tsx
<SsgoiTransitionBoundary scope={() => "products-layout"}>
  <ProductTabs />
  <SsgoiTransitionBoundary>{children}</SsgoiTransitionBoundary>
</SsgoiTransitionBoundary>
```

## 5. Bottom navigation and route groups

```text
app/
  layout.tsx                 # one SsgoiProvider
  (tabs)/
    layout.tsx               # stable shell + bottom nav
    page.tsx
    collections/page.tsx
    create/page.tsx
  (detail)/
    layout.tsx               # pathname boundary, no nav
    photo/[id]/page.tsx
```

```tsx
// app/(tabs)/layout.tsx
export default function TabsLayout({ children }) {
  return (
    <SsgoiTransitionBoundary scope={() => "tabs-shell"}>
      <SsgoiTransitionBoundary>
        {children}
      </SsgoiTransitionBoundary>
      <BottomNav />
    </SsgoiTransitionBoundary>
  );
}
```

```tsx
// app/(detail)/layout.tsx
export default function DetailLayout({ children }) {
  return <SsgoiTransitionBoundary>{children}</SsgoiTransitionBoundary>;
}
```

- Tab → tab: only inner content remounts; nav stays.
- Tab → detail: the `(tabs)` layout leaves; nav leaves with it.
- Detail → tab: the tab shell enters with the nav.

Full pattern: https://ssgoi.dev/llms/bottom-nav.txt

Route groups do not change URLs. Parallel and intercepted routes require
application-specific ownership. Use `useSelectedLayoutSegment()` when pathname
changes should not remount the active children slot.

## 6. Transition config

```ts
type SsgoiConfig = {
  transitions?: SsgoiTransitionRule[];
  middleware?: (from: string, to: string) => { from: string; to: string };
  preserveScroll?: PreserveScrollOption;
};
```

Rule forms:

```ts
{ on: "/posts/**", except: "/posts", transition: drill() }

{ from: "/gallery", to: "/gallery/:id", transition: zoom() }

{ ordered: ["/tabs/a", "/tabs/b"], transition: slide() }
```

- `on`: route family. Entering is forward; leaving is backward.
- `from`/`to`: precise pair. Reverse matching is enabled by default.
- `ordered`: direction comes from array order.
- `priority`: higher values win before path specificity.

Path patterns:

- `/posts`: exact path.
- `/posts/:id`: one named segment.
- `/posts/*`: exactly one arbitrary segment.
- `/posts/**`: `/posts` and every descendant.

`transitions` may depend on device context:

```ts
const config = {
  transitions: ({ isMobile }) =>
    isMobile
      ? [{ on: "/posts/**", transition: drill() }]
      : [{ on: "/posts/**", transition: fade() }],
};
```

## 7. Transition index

Use these links for effect-specific options.

- `fade`: unrelated pages and quiet cross-fades. https://ssgoi.dev/llms/fade.txt
- `drill`: list → detail hierarchy. https://ssgoi.dev/llms/drill.txt
- `slide`: ordered tabs and steps. https://ssgoi.dev/llms/slide.txt
- `axis`: sibling destinations with Material-style shared-axis motion. https://ssgoi.dev/llms/axis.txt
- `sheet`: compose, filters, and modal-like routes. https://ssgoi.dev/llms/sheet.txt
- `zoom`: card/image → detail expansion. https://ssgoi.dev/llms/zoom.txt
- `hero`: shared elements with page chrome transitions. https://ssgoi.dev/llms/hero.txt
- `scroll`: vertical sequences and editorial paging. https://ssgoi.dev/llms/scroll.txt
- `strip`: perspective strip flip. https://ssgoi.dev/llms/strip.txt
- `film`: cinematic gallery transition. https://ssgoi.dev/llms/film.txt
- `rotate`: card-like rotation. https://ssgoi.dev/llms/rotate.txt
- `blind`: window-blind reveal. https://ssgoi.dev/llms/blind.txt
- `jaemin`: playful branded transition. https://ssgoi.dev/llms/jaemin.txt

## 8. Other frameworks

### React Router

Use `useLocation()` and nested layout routes:

```tsx
const { pathname } = useLocation();

return (
  <div
    key={scope(pathname)}
    data-ssgoi-transition={pathname}
  >
    <Outlet />
  </div>
);
```

### TanStack Router

Use router state and parent routes:

```tsx
const pathname = useRouterState({
  select: (state) => state.location.pathname,
});
```

### SvelteKit

Use `+layout.svelte` for persistent chrome and route pages for inner markers.
Use a keyed block only when the layout must force a new DOM boundary.

```svelte
{#key resolveKey($page.url.pathname)}
  <div data-ssgoi-transition={$page.url.pathname}>
    {@render children()}
  </div>
{/key}
```

Guide: https://ssgoi.dev/llms/svelte.txt

### Nuxt / Vue

Use `useRoute()` and `:key="resolveKey(route.path)"`.

Guide: https://ssgoi.dev/llms/vue.txt

### SolidStart

Put `data-ssgoi-transition` on route roots. Persistent route layouts naturally
keep their outer DOM while child routes replace inner boundaries.

Guide: https://ssgoi.dev/llms/solid.txt

### Qwik City

Use `useSsgoi(root, { config$ })`. Qwik configs must be QRL factories. Put
transition attributes on route component roots under `<Slot />`.

Guide: https://ssgoi.dev/llms/qwik.txt

### Angular

Guide: https://ssgoi.dev/llms/angular.txt

## 9. Troubleshooting

No animation:

1. Confirm both routes are inside the same `<Ssgoi>`.
2. Confirm outgoing and incoming DOM nodes have transition attributes.
3. Confirm the rule matches both path values.
4. Confirm no pathname-keyed ancestor remounts a persistent inner layout.

Wrong region animates:

1. Find the nearest boundary whose key changed.
2. Keep persistent UI outside the inner boundary.
3. Put UI that must leave inside the outer boundary.
4. Use a stable scope key for routes sharing one layout.

Layout jumps:

1. Add `relative z-0` to the shell around `<Ssgoi>`.
2. Add `overflow-x-clip` for horizontal effects.
3. Give route boundaries a full-height background.

Reference templates:

- Next.js: https://github.com/meursyphus/ssgoi/tree/main/templates/nextjs
- React Router: https://github.com/meursyphus/ssgoi/tree/main/templates/react-router
- TanStack Router: https://github.com/meursyphus/ssgoi/tree/main/templates/tanstack-router
- SvelteKit: https://github.com/meursyphus/ssgoi/tree/main/templates/sveltekit
- Nuxt: https://github.com/meursyphus/ssgoi/tree/main/templates/nuxt
- SolidStart: https://github.com/meursyphus/ssgoi/tree/main/templates/solidstart
- Qwik City: https://github.com/meursyphus/ssgoi/tree/main/templates/qwik
